issues.item: Threat: Risky Behavior: Taking too many risks or doing things that could cause you harm
issues.explanation: Risky behavior is hard to reconcile with the rest of the threat profile, which is dominated by fear-based hypervigilance and exaggerated startle. In this profile it introduces a more externalizing response pattern that is not supported elsewhere in memory, appraisals, triggers, or strategies.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Betrayal: I was betrayed by someone I trusted
issues.explanation: Betrayal by a trusted person does not fit well with the stated trauma type of civilian in a war zone unless there is evidence of an interpersonal betrayal trauma, which is otherwise absent from the profile. The rest of the items center on war exposure, victims, grief, loss of control, and danger rather than trusted-person betrayal.

issues.item: Triggers: Victim Memories: Reminders of victims
issues.explanation: Reminders of victims fit war-zone exposure, but paired with perpetrator-focused avoidance and betrayal appraisals they imply a specific interpersonal-harm narrative that is not otherwise coherently represented. The profile oscillates between mass-trauma civilian exposure and a perpetrator-betrayal formulation.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Avoid Perpetrator Cues: Anything that reminds me of the person who harmed me
issues.explanation: Avoiding cues related to the person who harmed me implies a discrete perpetrator-centered trauma. That is difficult to integrate with the rest of the profile, which more strongly reflects civilian war-zone exposure, victims, grief, and generalized threat rather than a single identifiable assailant.

vignette: Rohan had always been proud of his work as a painter, taking joy in transforming blank walls into vibrant works of art. But since his experience as a civilian in a war zone five years ago, the world had become a very different place for him. The smell of turpentine, once a familiar and comforting scent, now transported him back to the moment when an explosion rocked the market where he was shopping. The sound of bangs or loud noises made him jump, his heart racing as if he were still dodging gunfire. As Rohan navigated his daily routine, these triggers set off a chain reaction. He became hypervigilant, constantly on guard against potential threats, and his body felt tense and ready to react at all times. He would ruminate about the event, replaying it over and over in his mind, trying to make sense of why it had happened to him. "Why was I there that day?" he would ask himself, as if answering this question could somehow undo the trauma. The memories themselves were still vivid, and when they came flooding back, Rohan's body would reenact the same position he had been in during the explosion - curled up, trying to shield himself from harm. The grief he felt upon recalling that day was overwhelming, leaving him breathless and disbelieving. "It feels like it didn't really happen," he would say, shaking his head. Rohan's experience had also profoundly changed his outlook on life. He no longer saw the world as a place of beauty and possibility but rather as a treacherous landscape full of hidden dangers. This negative appraisal had seeped into every aspect of his life, making him feel lost and without purpose. He felt he was no longer capable of doing the things that defined him - creating art, spending time with loved ones - because the world was too unpredictable. In an attempt to cope with these feelings, Rohan threw himself into his work, using busyness as a shield against the memories and emotions that threatened to overwhelm him. He also began avoiding news reports about similar events, fearing they would trigger another cycle of rumination and hypervigilance. However, this strategy only served to further reinforce his negative appraisals, making it harder for him to shake off the feeling that he was living in a state of constant threat. As time went on, Rohan found himself withdrawing from social interactions, avoiding friends and family who reminded him of the life he once had. His marriage began to suffer, as his wife struggled to understand why he couldn't simply "move on" from the past. The more Rohan tried to push away the memories, the more they seemed to haunt him, until it felt like he was living in a never-ending nightmare. Despite his best efforts, Rohan couldn't shake off the feeling that he was stuck in this cycle of trauma and avoidance. He knew he needed help but was afraid of confronting the demons that had taken up residence in his mind. It wasn't until he found himself unable to sleep, his body tense with anticipation, waiting for the next explosion or trigger, that Rohan realized he couldn't keep living like this. With a heavy heart, he made the decision to seek help, hoping against hope that somehow, someway, he could learn to heal and find peace once more.
